UC researchers identify viral processes key to broader coronavirus treatments

October 28, 2026
Breast Cancer Awareness Month Q&A
Breast cancer is one of the most common cancers in the United States, affecting around 1 in 8 women according to the American Cancer Society. With incidence rates continuing to increase by around 1% per year, Breast Cancer Awareness Month each October promotes awareness and early detection of the disease.
Read More »
October 27, 2026
Lightening the Load: The SOM Office of Faculty Development
During a routine doctor’s appointment, Kay Monteith was chatting with her physician about her job. Monteith, who had recently joined the UC Riverside School of Medicine’s Office of Faculty Development at the time, described her new role as an instructional designer. “I said I take the doctors’ PowerPoints and make them a little bit easier to learn or enjoyable to look at,” Monteith recalled.
Her physician’s reply was simple yet heartfelt: “Thank you.”
Read More »
October 23, 2026
Bjorkman Speaks on New Vaccine Techniques to Prevent the Next Pandemic
In the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic, researchers shifted their focus towards preventing the next possible pandemic by developing the next generation of vaccines to provide protection against a broad base of coronaviruses. On Thursday, Oct. 22, 2026, Pamela Bjorkman, PhD, of the California Institute of Technology shared some of the recent breakthroughs in vaccine development at the Thomas and Salma Haider Biomedical Breakthrough Lecture at the UC Riverside School of Medicine.
Read More »
October 20, 2026
UCR welcomes new faculty members
Riverside welcomed 31 new permanent faculty members from a variety of disciplines for the 2026-27 academic year.
Read More »
October 16, 2026
Child Mental Health is Improving, but Still Work to be Done
In a Grand Rounds presentation at the UC Riverside School of Medicine titled “Five Years Later: Progress, Partnerships, and Possibilities in Child Mental Health,” psychiatrist Tami Benton, MD, said that American youth are showing the first drop in emotional distress in more than a decade, but that there is still more work to be done in ensuring young people have access to proper mental health care.
Read More »
October 16, 2026
Gauging the Inland Empire’s well-being
UC Riverside’s Center for Community Solutions will survey 1,000 adults in Riverside and San Bernardino counties to inform strategies to improve life in the Inland Empire, thanks to a grant from the IEHP Foundation, an Inland Empire health advocacy nonprofit.
Residents will be asked about their experiences with nutrition, housing, health care, transportation, employment, education, access to recreation, the environment, and other factors that shape their well-being.
Read More »
October 14, 2026
A Fund to Help Future Highlanders: The Rasyidi Family Endowed Scholarship Fund
When physicians answer immediate questions about patient care, they fall back on their experience--and their medical education. “You'll get a call at 2 am where the nurse has a very clear question: ‘Their most recent blood count came back at this, what should I do?’” recalled UCR alumnus Ernest Rasyidi, MD. “That's not your time to be like, ‘let me go to a textbook’--either you know it or you don't,” he added.
